Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Raleigh NC
656 AM EDT Mon Sep 14 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...

* Temperatures trending a few degrees cooler for Tuesday morning 
  into Wednesday morning.

* Precipitation chances late week into the weekend continue to
  trend down with the return of convective chances being pushed
  later into early next week.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 230 AM Monday...

1) Seasonable and drier conditions Tues through Wed night with 
unseasonably warm weather returning late week into the weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 230 AM Monday...

KEY MESSAGE 1... Seasonable and drier conditions Tues through 
Wed night with unseasonably warm weather returning late week 
into the weekend.

A surface cold front is still slowly working its way through 
the lower Ohio Valley and northern Mid-Atlantic based on the 06z
observations. Ahead of this front however, a pre-frontal 
trough, roughly around the I-95 corridor, is slowly ushering in 
slightly drier air across the Piedmont and slowly advancing 
eastward. Model guidance continues to push the cold front into 
and through our region from the north-northeast as a backdoor 
cold front through peak heating into this evening. Thankfully, 
drier air mixing down to the surface behind the pre-frontal 
trough (mean mixing-ratio at 00z GSO RAOB 13.4 compared to 17.7 
at MHX) will greatly limit instability along and ahead of the 
front this afternoon. Isolated sprinkles or a shower or two 
can't be ruled out, especially across the Sandhills and 
southern/central Coastal Plain where favorable diurnal timing, 
500-1500 J/kg of SBCAPE, and glancing influence from trough axis
pivoting across and offshore of the northern Mid-Atlantic may 
overcome marginal instability and drier mid/upper-lvl air. 

A prolonged period of minimal convective chances is expected 
behind the frontal passage as a seasonably significant mid/upper
lvl subtropical ridge (+2.5 to 3 standardized height anomalies 
from 850 to 200mb Tues through Thurs night) builds over the TN 
Valley and southern Appalachians; perhaps even reaching 600 dam
at H5 by Wed. A brief dip down to seasonable temperatures is 
expected post cold-frontal passage Tues and perhaps lingering 
into Wed before moderating back to 10-15 degrees above normal as
the ridge flattens and anomalous H85 temps sag south into the 
Carolinas into the weekend. Forecast uncertainty remains on when
convective chances return to the region as how/when the 
anomalous ridge loosens its grip over the Carolinas remains 
highly inconsistent among NWP models; below normal PoPs may 
linger until late this weekend into early next week.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
As of 655 AM Monday...

Prevailing northwest winds after sunrise will veer out of the north-
northeast behind a backdoor cold front with frequent gusts of around 
15 kts, especially at RWI, FAY and as far west as RDU through the 
afternoon into the evening. Pressure rises continuing after 23z may 
continue periodic gustiness for a few hours after sunset, mainly 
around FAY. Low-VFR cigs, sprinkles, and perhaps a brief shower may 
be possible around the Triad terminals after 00z into Tues morning.

Outlook: Prevailing VFR conditions expected as deep high pressure 
persists over the region through at least Friday.

&&

.RAH WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
None.

&&

$$

AVIATION...AS

FXUS62 KILM 141033
AFDILM

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Wilmington NC
630 AM EDT Mon Sep 14 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Rain chances for this evening should remain limited to coastal 
areas and offshore waters as the cold front moves through the 
region. A stray shower is possible late this afternoon, but hi-
res guidance remains inconsistent. Confidence remains high that 
near-record high temperatures are expected today and significant
relief will follow.

Aviation section updated. 

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1) Unseasonable heat may break record highs at Wilmington and 
Myrtle Beach Monday. A shower is possible ahead of a cold front 
this evening.

2) A modified Canadian airmass will bring cooler temperatures 
and drier conditions to the area beginning late Monday night.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1... Unseasonable heat may break record highs at 
Wilmington and Myrtle Beach Monday. A shower is possible ahead 
of a cold front this evening.

Temperatures should rise into the 90s one last time Monday. A 
surface trough should drift offshore early Monday morning 
leaving light northwesterly winds in place throughout the day. 
This will hold the seabreeze back and allow hot air to push all 
the way down to the beaches. Our forecast high of 94 in 
Wilmington would tie the record set back in 2010, and our 
forecast high of 92 at North Myrtle Beach would break the record
set back in 2020. Florence and Lumberton should remain a few 
degrees shy of their records. Heat indices are forecast to top 
out in the upper 90s to around 100 inland, with some 101-103 
readings possible within higher dewpoints near the coast.

Warm temperatures and convergence along the sea breeze may
produce a stray shower during the afternoon. However, dry air 
aloft will be a challenge for any developing convection. Rain 
chances increase later in the afternoon ahead of a cold front as
surface lift taps into the warm and humid surface layer. 
Showers will be more focused near the coast and offshore where 
surface moisture is greatest. CAMs are inconsistent on the 
extent of showers, but latest HREF keeps PoPs low throughout the
day and maximizes rain chances during the frontal passage near
the coast. Favored this distribution for the latest forecast.

KEY MESSAGE 2... A modified Canadian airmass will bring cooler 
temperatures and drier conditions to the area beginning late
Monday night.

A refreshing surge of cooler, drier northeast winds will spread
in behind the front Monday night. Daytime highs Tuesday through
Thursday should remain in the 80s, but the real change will be
apparent with overnight lows. For locations away from the
coast, forecast lows are in the 60s Monday night through 
Friday night. 

Our forecast low Tuesday night in Wilmington is 64, the coolest
in over 3 months!

&&

.AVIATION /12Z MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
VFR through the TAF period. Patchy ground fog could result in a 
brief period of sub-VFR restrictions, mainly near the coast. A cold 
front will drop southward on Monday evening. A few showers or storms 
will be possible ahead of the front during the late afternoon, but 
chances are low. Winds will shift to the NE and intensify behind the 
front. Dry air should maintain VFR conditions.

Extended Outlook... VFR conditions should persist through 
Friday in a drier and cooler airmass.

&&

.MARINE...
Northerly winds develop across the region early Monday morning.
During the afternoon, differential heating should produce a 
strong enough sea breeze for winds near the coast to turn 
southeasterly. A few storms are possible during the afternoon, 
but rain chances increase this evening as a cold front plunges 
southward. Northeast winds surge behind the front this evening. 
The surge of northeasterly winds behind the front is expected to
reach 20-25 knots across the Cape Fear coastal waters and a 
Small Craft Advisory remains in effect. Slightly weaker winds
are expected for portions of the SC nearshore waters early 
Tuesday. Breezy northeast winds should continue through at least
Tuesday evening before weakening somewhat by Wednesday. 
Directions should remain east to northeast through Thursday.

&&

.ILM WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
NC...None.
SC...None.
MARINE...Small Craft Advisory from 8 PM this evening to noon EDT 
     Tuesday for AMZ250-252.

&&

$$

AFDJAX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Jacksonville FL
743 AM EDT Mon Sep 14 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

For the latest NE FL and SE GA Daily Key Messages please visit:
https:/www.weather.gov/media/jax/briefings/nws-jax-briefing.pdf

- Moderate Rip Current Risk all Local Beaches Today and Friday.
Elevated Risk Returns Early Next Week

- Daily Heat Index up to 107 through Sunday

- Daily Afternoon & Evening Thunderstorms. Main Hazards: Locally
Heavy Rain, Lightning & Gusty Winds Up to 40-50 mph

&&

.NEAR TERM /THROUGH TONIGHT/...
Main Highlights This Period: 

- Highest Thunderstorm Chances South of I-95 Corridor, Mainly North 
  Central Florida

- Heat Index Near Heat Advisory Today


Prevailing flow will transition into a more onshore flow pattern 
today with surface winds shifting to become more out of the 
northeast and east during the late evening and overnight hours. 
Drier air associated with high pressure to the north will settle 
across southeast Georgia today and then advance southward into 
northeast Florida later tonight, with the dissipating coastal trough 
being moved westward into the gulf. Convection will be inhibited 
over southeast Georgia today with the highest likelihood for showers 
and storms occurring over north central Florida and for areas along 
and south of the I-10 corridor. High temperatures this afternoon 
will reach up into the lower to mid 90s over inland areas and in the 
upper 80s and lower 90s along the coast. Overnight low temperatures 
will drop down into the the lower to mid 70s for inland areas and in 
the upper 70s for coastal areas and along the St Johns River. Heat 
index values for this afternoon will rise to over 105-107 for 
portions of northeast Florida, however heat advisory levels are not 
expected to occur prior to the development of diurnal convection.

&&

.SHORT TERM /TUESDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY NIGHT/...
Main Highlights This Period: 

- A high rip current risk and rough surf likely for area beaches 
  starting Tuesday and last through at least Thursday.

- Breezy northeast winds begins Tuesday, continues through Thursday. 
  A wind advisory is possible for the immediate coast Tuesday and 
  Wednesday.

A backdoor cold front will push through the area Tuesday as strong 
high pressure builds to the northeast. A surge of northeast and east 
winds will move south over the region. Strongest winds will be for 
the coastal counties with speeds up to 15-25 mph and 10-15 mph well 
inland. A wind advisory is possible for the immediate coast due to 
the breezy winds. A chance of showers and embedded storms expected 
Tuesday due to low level convergence and ample moisture. Best rain 
chances will be for the coastal areas at 50-60 percent and about 20 
percent for the far western zones. Some chance for a few showers 
will exist Tuesday night into Wednesday morning especially for the 
coast, but overall a drier airmass will filter into the area with 
PWATs dropping to about 1.1 to 1.6 inches.  

For Wednesday, strong 500 mb high pressure system remains fixed over 
eastern TN, but retrogrades as a well-defined mid to upper level low 
over the western Atlantic moves to the north Bahamas late Wednesday. 
This will continue to enhance the low level pressure gradient 
continuing the breezy northeast winds over the area with a more 
stable airmass in place. A small chance of showers (about 10-20 
percent) will continue due to the breezy flow off the warm Atlantic 
waters, but thunder chances are sub 15 percent. For wind headlines, 
a wind advisory will be possible for the immediate coast.

Temperatures will be above normal by 1-3 degrees Tuesday, but trend 
lower to about average levels on Wednesday. For lows Tuesday night, 
a cooling trend is noted with lows in the upper 60s for inland 
southeast GA, but 70s most everywhere else. Lows trend a bit cooler 
Wednesday night with the mid to upper 60s for inland areas from I-10 
northward and mostly lower to mid 70s elsewhere.

&&

.LONG TERM /THURSDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
Main Highlights This Period: 

- Daily chances for showers and thunderstorms
- Elevated rip current risk and rough surf for area beaches will 
continue this period

The mid to upper level low pressure/TUTT feature noted earlier will 
be passing over the FL peninsula on Thursday while the strong mid 
level high pressure ridge is situated across mid MS valley to the TN 
valley. The TUTT feature will likely enhance rain chances, due to 
increased moisture and instability, from Thursday onward, as the 
TUTT feature shifts westward, ending up in the central Gulf by 
Saturday. As the TUTT feature moves away for the weekend, low to mid 
level high pressure will ease off the Carolina coast and into the 
western Atlantic this weekend. 

For Thursday, still breezy for coastal areas, and good rain chances 
for the coastal zones and as well as inland northeast FL. For Friday 
into the weekend, rain chances increase to scattered to possibly 
numerous coverage for most counties with less of a pressure gradient 
resulting in weaker surface winds generally from the east and at 
times southeast as the sfc high pressure moves off to the northeast 
to east of the area.

Temperatures will trend around average this period.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z MONDAY THROUGH 12Z TUESDAY/...

VFR conditions with scattered to broken mid clouds around 
6-8kft as of 12z. VFR will maintain through at KSSI and SE GA 
terminals through tonight, with little convective activity 
expected while other sites across NE FL will have potential for 
TSRA impacts this afternoon with SHRA possible as early as 16z. 
The highest potential for +TSRA and associated gusty winds and 
LIFR/IFR visibility restrictions will be along the I-75 corridor
(KGNV/KOCF/KLCQ) between 20-24z today. Activity will generally 
move southwestward through the early evening and diminish after 
00z. Surface winds will trend WNW at or below 10 knots until the
easterly sea breeze pushes inland this afternoon. A backdoor 
front will reach the area Tuesday morning brining the potential 
for MVFR to IFR stratocumulus, gusty northeasterly winds 
(especially at the coast) and waves of scattered showers and 
isolated Thunderstorms through Tuesday.

&&

.MARINE...


Offshore winds will continue across area waters today with the 
exception of sea breeze winds developing from the east during the 
afternoon hours. Less thunderstorm activity is expected for today 
and will likely be limited to northeast Florida nearshore waters.
From Tuesday through Thursday, a strong northeast wind surge will 
bring small craft advisory conditions, rough seas, and numerous 
showers and a few thunderstorms over the area waters. Improving 
conditions are expected by Friday as onshore winds weaken and seas 
gradually lower.

Rip Currents: Prevailing offshore winds (excepting for the afternoon 
sea breeze) and weak easterly swells will keep a low-end moderate 
risk of rip currents in effect for today. By Tuesday, strengthening 
northeast winds and building surf combine to lead to dangerous surf 
and a high rip current risk area beaches starting for 
Tuesday, and through at least Thursday.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
     PATCHY TO AREAS OF HIGH DISPERSIONS TUESDAY THROUGH THURSDAY 
- Afternoons

Weak troughing over the area will dissipate today. Strong high 
pressure will build to the northeast as a backdoor cool front moves 
through on Tuesday. Strong high pressure remains north of the area 
Wednesday into Thursday. Much higher winds begin by midday Tuesday 
for the coastal areas with speeds up to 15 to 20 mph, gusting to 30-
35 mph. These elevated winds remain in place for Wednesday and 
possibly into Thursday, especially at the coast. The high pressure 
north of the area will weaken Friday, with another high building to 
the northeast over the weekend. Strong surface and transport winds 
will lead to areas of high daytime dispersion for the Tuesday to 
Thursday time frame.

A chance of showers and thunderstorms today, mainly inland northeast 
Florida. Higher chances of showers and a few embedded thunderstorms 
for coastal zones Tuesday. 

Fog Potential...Patchy fog is expected early this morning mainly 
across inland northeast FL. Some patchy fog is possible late 
tonight/early Tuesday morning inland areas.

&&

.PRELIMINARY POINT TEMPS/POPS...
AMG  94  73  91  69 /  10   0  30   0 
SSI  92  79  88  76 /  10   0  50  10 
JAX  92  75  90  73 /  30   0  50  20 
SGJ  90  77  88  76 /  20  20  60  40 
GNV  93  73  91  73 /  50  20  50   0 
OCF  93  74  92  74 /  70  20  60   0 

&&

.JAX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
FL...None.
GA...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

FXUS65 KBOU 141126
AFDBOU

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Denver/Boulder CO
526 AM MDT Mon Sep 14 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Still very warm today, with isolated to scattered showers and a
  couple storms. Mostly light precipitation amounts. 

- Unsettled pattern rest of this week, but plenty of uncertainty
  with regard to daily precipitation chances. Thursday still looks
  like the highest opportunity of measurable rain (50-70%), and a
  locally heavy rainfall threat. 

- Cooler weather arriving for Tuesday. Temperatures bounce back
  Wednesday, but then average around seasonal normals through next
  weekend. 

&&

.DISCUSSION /Through Sunday/...
Issued at 222 AM MDT Mon Sep 14 2026

Satellite shows a weak shortwave pushing across Colorado in these
early morning hours, with scattered showers and a couple
thunderstorms along and ahead of it. While these will attempt to 
move onto the plains this morning with the associated lift, most 
of these will weaken or dissipate in the downslope westerly flow 
aloft. That stronger flow develops today as a deeper upper level 
low tracks across the Northern Rockies. Water vapor imagery  
indicates drying behind our first shortwave, so the chances of 
precipitation are generally decreasing after this early morning
disturbance. That said, we will still have some low level 
moisture and weak instability (MLCAPE 500 J/kg or less) over the 
western slope and plains mainly southeast of I-76. That's where 
we'll keep the highest PoPs (30-40%), but lower PoPs (10-20%) 
elsewhere. Temperatures will still be quite warm given downslope 
flow, and increasing westerly breezes. In fact, some gusts near 50
mph can be expected over the Front Range mountains, with a few
gusts (outside of showers) to around 30 mph possibly reaching
Boulder. The stronger downslope component should boost highs to near
90F across the plains for one last time this season (Denver has 
had a total 65 90F degree days, the 4th most 90s since records 
began in 1872).

Cooler weather arrives tonight as a cold front pushes across the 
plains by or shortly after midnight. How much cooler for Tuesday 
is still in question. The latest data indicates low level 
moisture and thus stratus potential or extent of any low clouds 
behind the front would be lacking, so we'll likely have more 
sunshine and thus be able to reach the lower to mid 70s over most 
of the plains and I-25 Corridor. The lack of low level moisture 
also means our precipitation chances, at least in the lower 
elevations, will be limited. Mountain areas should fare better 
with at least scattered shower/storm coverage given monsoonal 
moisture builds again in southwest flow aloft. 

Stronger ridging occurs Wednesday as the next upper level closed 
low digs southward along the Pacific coast. This means warmer 
temperatures with highs likely pushing back into the mid 80s for 
the lower elevations. Once again, the highest shower and storm 
chances will occur for the mountains given increasing moisture and
instability during the day, while the plains reside in a more 
marginal environment for convection given warming aloft but some 
moisture still available.

Thursday is still shaping up to be the most active day with an
embedded shortwave and deeper monsoonal moisture lifting 
northeast across the forecast area. Precipitable water values 
will likely range from 150-200% of normal, so can't rule out 
locally heavy rain. WPC Excessive Rainfall Outlook has portions of
our forecast area in Slight Risk, and this seems reasonable, 
especially if we are able to moisten up the low levels. 

There remains plenty of uncertainty in the forecast through next
weekend, as there is little confidence in the timing of the West
Coast trough eventually lift east/northeast across the Northern
and Central Rockies. As a result, this period remains rather 
broad-brushed at this point, with continued chances of showers 
and storms and temperatures averaging near normal. 

&&

.AVIATION /12Z TAFS through 12Z Tuesday/...
Issued at 526 AM MDT Mon Sep 14 2026

A few light showers had developed in the area, and some of these
have been producing enhanced SW-W gusts to 20-25 kts. We'll keep
the PROB30 in the forecast til around 16Z, but also added gusty
winds to 20+ kts in that PROB group. Ceilings will stay well above
6000 feet. Confidence is increasing somewhat about the winds
becoming W-NW (>60% chance) by 15Z-16Z, given passage of 
disturbance and sufficient downslope gradient off the Front Range.
Most models are coming around to at least a few hours of that 
15Z-19Z, but then potentially becoming variable (30% chance)
19Z-24Z versus a continuation of W-NW (30% chance) or a 
transition to light northerly (40% chance). 

Also, while the chance of showers is limited due to lack of 
instability, it will still be quite warm with high DCAPE. As a 
result, we'll keep the PROB30 with VRB G30kts in the TAFS for the 
21Z-01Z period. Cold front will arrive around 06Z Tuesday, which 
would bring a low threat (20% chance) of stratus impacts for the 
Tuesday morning rush. A period of gusty N winds to around 20-25
kts expected with the front, then decreasing by 10Z-12Z. 

&&

.BOU WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
None.

&&

$$
